added_lemmas.justification: The two-point calculation uses only one exact fixed-design independent Mat\'ern-one-half subexperiment, so the lower bounds are monotone under inclusion of that subexperiment.
added_lemmas.gap: Broader spatial model classes inherit the converse only after their observation experiment, deterministic design sequence, response law, and common slope interval are shown to contain the specified subexperiment.
added_lemmas.consumer: This conditional transfer separates the narrow-class upper theory from the more robust scope of the root-\(N\) length and \(N^{-1}\) risk converse.

prose_updates.tldr: Three exact affine-annihilating local slopes reduce the stated signed Mat\'ern cross-tail model to a finite-dimensional mean cone and yield uniform actual-design Gaussian inference through vanishing amplitude. On the narrow parametric Gaussian, quasi-uniform, no-nugget class, the profile construction has asymptotic observed-law coverage, root-\(N\) diameter, and root-\(N\) estimation risk. An exact complete-data Gaussian two-point argument matches the diameter and squared-risk rates; its converse transfers conditionally to every superclass that contains the same fixed-design independent Mat\'ern-one-half \(A=0\) subexperiment with a common nontrivial slope interval. The exact least-favorable critical value is mathematically attained; the sole residual open question is a terminating certified numerical approximation of its continuum maximum with a proved error bound.

project_justification.gap: Published spatial-confounding results identify or consistently estimate slopes under local spectral separation, and published fixed-domain results provide inference for selected covariance functionals. They do not deliver the stated design-uniform profile inference through a cross-tail local to zero. Nor does a broad covariance class inherit this note's upper theorem merely from containing similar Mat\'ern models; the upper expansion requires the precise signed-cross-tail, Gaussian, quasi-uniform, no-nugget structure used here.
project_justification.niche: The narrow upper model isolates a nonregular finite-dimensional nuisance geometry in which three scales separate \(\beta\) uniformly and affine filters control actual irregular designs in dimensions one and two. The converse is structurally more robust: it uses only an exact fixed-design independent Mat\'ern-one-half \(A=0\) subexperiment and therefore transfers to any statistical superclass once that subexperiment, the observation law, and a common nontrivial slope interval are verified.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the actual-design Gaussian experiment, feasible residual-scale studentization, exact mathematically attained least-favorable calibration, asymptotic observed-law coverage, root-\(N\) diameter and risk, and matching honest lower bounds on the stated class. A conditional superclass corollary formalizes converse monotonicity without enlarging the scope of the upper theorem. Certified effective computation of the continuum critical value remains the sole residual open question.

prose_updates.related_work: Guan, Page, Reich, Ventrucci and Yang motivate high-frequency adjustment for spatial confounding, but their two-dimensional noisy/common-range or parsimonious formulations differ from the exact fixed-design independent Mat\'ern-one-half, no-nugget subexperiment used in this converse; no automatic model-class inclusion is claimed. Datta and Stein characterize consistent infill estimability and construct local-difference and Laplacian estimators over broader Gaussian-field settings. Their framework is a candidate application of the superclass lower-bound transfer only if its observation scheme, deterministic design sequence, response construction, common slope interval, and inclusion of the exact \(A=0\) subexperiment are verified from that model; this match is not asserted here. Keshavarz, Nguyen and Scott provide irregular-lattice quadratic-form Gaussian theory, Loh, Sun and Wen develop higher-order variations on selected irregular designs, and Lim and Stein analyze filtered spatial cross-periodograms; these works inform the narrow-class upper proof but do not broaden its scope. Zhang and Li supply scalar Mat\'ern microergodic context, while Andrews and Mikusheva inform weak-identification calibration. Burman, Ogburn and Datta remain the conditional PM2.5 and COVID-19 county-centroid consumer when the stated Mat\'ern, no-nugget, and quasi-uniform-design diagnostics hold.
prose_updates.honest_scope: All achievability claims---the actual-design Gaussian experiment, feasible studentization, profile confidence sets, exact mathematically attained calibration, asymptotic observed-law coverage, and root-\(N\) upper diameter and risk---remain restricted to the stated signed bivariate Mat\'ern, stationary Gaussian, deterministic quasi-uniform, no-nugget class in dimensions one and two. The lower bound is proved there and transfers conditionally to any statistical superclass containing the same fixed-design independent Mat\'ern-one-half \(A=0\) observed experiment over a common nontrivial slope interval. No such inclusion is asserted automatically for Guan et al.; Datta--Stein is only a candidate application pending explicit verification of the observation scheme, design sequence, response construction, and submodel inclusion. The scope excludes nuggets, unknown marginal-smoothness adaptation, nonstationarity, independent Fourier-coordinate approximations, and broader covariance classes for the upper result. The sole residual open question is \texttt{oeq:certified-attainable-critical-value-computation}: a terminating certified numerical approximation, with a proved error bound, of the continuum attainable critical value. The county-centroid application remains conditional on the model and design diagnostics and does not by itself establish a broader nonparametric causal estimand.

statement_notes.justification: The exact complete observed-field Gaussian likelihood on an independent \(A=0\) subexperiment gives bounded total variation for \(N^{-1/2}\)-separated slopes without identifying \(p\).
statement_notes.gap: Scalar microergodic limits and abstract modulus theory do not by themselves prove honest expected-length or squared-risk lower bounds for arbitrary procedures in the complete bivariate observed experiment.
statement_notes.consumer: The theorem matches the narrow-class upper rates; \texttt{prop:superclass-honest-lower-bound} is its superclass corollary and transfers only the converse to any class for which the exact embedded subexperiment is verified.
